reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 a PICTURE that combines a floating insertion string (cs, '+' or '-') with zero suppression ('Z' or '*') must be refused, and one that uses both 'Z' and '*' must be refused, while fixed insertion beside zero suppression stays legal.

edition-consulted.switches: dialectLevel < 2002: a non-floating currency symbol takes only the CurrencyLeading role (the 1985 chart has one fixed cs row/column); also appends the 1985 chart clause to the COBOL1935 message
edition.DialectLevel < 2002 selects the 1985 BLANK WHEN ZERO arm (asterisk only, VI.5.9.3 SR7) over the 2002+ S-or-asterisk arm; message text

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry/CobolVersion in PictureComposition.cs and PictureAnalyzer.cs. The cells that decide this rule (floating {+-}/cs rows and columns against {Z *}) are the 2023 Table 10 matrix used at every edition; compared by hand with the 1985 chart of VI.5.9.6 (spec md lines 11449-11471): the floating {Z*}-left row is blank in every floating +-/cs column, the floating {+-}-left and cs-left rows are blank in the {Z*} columns, the same as Table10Rows. SR21 (Z/* exclusive) and SR23 (+/- exclusive) are edition-blind.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the floating-vs-suppression and Z-vs-* refusals are the same code and the same matrix cells at 1985 and 2023 (probes 1 and 8 give the same diagnostic at --std 2023).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb528 and pb530 are legal-source witnesses only (ZZ9, ***9, $$$9.99, ZZZ,ZZ9.99, +$$$); no witness of the refusal half (floating with Z/*, Z with *)

probes.printed: $$$ZZ9, ZZ$$$9, ++ZZ9, ZZ++9, --**9, **--9, $$**9: error COBOL1935 (the Table-10 precedence pair named); ZZ**9, **ZZ9: error COBOL1934 'the symbol Z and the symbol * are mutually exclusive'
probes.expected: each refused: floating insertion and zero suppression are mutually exclusive; only one replacement type with zero suppression
legal: fixed insertion is not floating insertion

probes.printed: CURRENCY SIGN IS "E", PIC EEZZ9: error COBOL1935 Z may not follow E
probes.expected: refused at 1985: a floating currency string of the 1985 currency letter E with zero suppression

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR3  (5.9.5 Editing Rules)  the text is in GR3
OK  §1985:VI.5.9.6  (5.9.6 Precedence Rules)  the text is in the clause

reader.notes: Floating-vs-suppression is refused by the Table-10 walk (its floating and Z/* cells match the 1985 chart), and Z-vs-* by SR21; fixed insertion beside suppression stays legal. The diagnostics cite §2023 clauses at --std 85 (COBOL1934 adds no 1985 citation), which is wording, not a conformance failure.

refuter.evidence: g1..g64 at --std 85 beyond the reader's set: floating vs suppression on both sides of the point and in both orders refused (ZZ++, **$$, $$**, ZZ--9, $$.ZZ, ++.**, $$$.**, Z$Z, *$$9, +$$**, $(3)Z(2) COBOL1935; Z,ZZ9.++, ZZ.$$, **.++, **.$$ COBOL1934); Z with * refused in every arrangement incl. lowercase z and insertion between (z*9, ZZ*9, **z9, ZB*9, Z.**, *.ZZ, Z(3)*(2)9 COBOL1934); fixed insertion beside suppression stays legal and renders per GR6 (+**9 [+**1], **9+ [**1+], $**.** [$*1.00], +$**9 [+$**1], 0**9 [0*12], -ZZ.ZZ, ZZ.ZZ-). The 1985 chart (spec md 11449-11471) has blanks at every floating{+-}/cs x {Z*} cell; no probe found a combination the compiler admits. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.9.5 GR3  (5.9.5 Editing Rules)  the text is in GR3'.
